title: An Iterator Over a Search Tree

concept.title: Keep the left road on a stack and take values one at a time
body: An *iterator* gives the values of a collection one by one, in order, without building the whole list first. For a binary search tree the order is the in-order one (increasing). The iterative in-order walk already has the right shape: it keeps a **stack** with the road of nodes going left from the root. The top of the stack is always the **next** value.
To move on: pop the top node, give its value, and then push the left road of its **right child**, because the nodes of the right subtree come next.

body.code:
stack = []
node = root
while node:                      # start: the left road from the root
    stack.append(node)
    node = node.left

def has_next():
    return len(stack) > 0

def next_value():
    top = stack.pop()
    node = top.right             # the right subtree comes after this node
    while node:
        stack.append(node)
        node = node.left
    return top.val

body: Each node is pushed and popped once, so any series of `n` calls to `next` costs O(n) in total (O(1) on average per call), and the stack holds at most the height of the tree, so the memory is O(h). Building the full sorted list would also work but needs O(n) memory, which is exactly what an iterator avoids.

statement: A binary search tree is given, and then a list of operations on its in-order iterator, which starts before the smallest value. `next` moves the iterator to the next value in increasing order and prints it. `has` prints `yes` if there is still a value after the current position and `no` if not. Print one line for every operation.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
The third line has `q`, the number of operations.
The fourth line has `q` words, each `next` or `has`.
outputFormat: One line for every operation: the value for `next`, `yes` or `no` for `has`.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.
The tree is a binary search tree (all values are different).
`next` is used only when there is a next value, and at least one operation is `next`.

examples.note: The values come in the order 1 2 3: next prints 1, has prints yes, next prints 2, next prints 3, has prints no.

hints: Keep a stack with the nodes on the road that goes left from the root.
The top of the stack is the next value.
After taking a node from the stack, push the left road of its right child.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def run(root, ops):
    stack = []
    node = root
    while node is not None:
        stack.append(node)
        node = node.left
    out = []
    for op in ops:
        if op == "next":
            top = stack.pop()
            out.append(str(top.val))
            node = top.right
            while node is not None:
                stack.append(node)
                node = node.left
        else:
            out.append("yes" if stack else "no")
    return out

t = int(input())
vals = input().split()
q = int(input())
ops = input().split()

print("\n".join(run(build_tree(vals), ops)))
